title: The Ghost of Geneva
premise: Paloma Hartwell, a disgraced intelligence analyst now working deniable cases from Geneva, is hired to trace a private jet that vanished mid-flight—every transponder log, passenger manifest, and radar record erased while the aircraft was still airborne. Her investigation leads to Elias Voss, a defector carrying proof that the flight was erased to smuggle out evidence of an inherited criminal fortune laundered through three generations of a banking dynasty. As Paloma realizes Voss himself may be bait designed to flush out everyone who knows about the flight, she must move him across a border checkpoint during a shift change, trading her hard-won invisibility for a public act of justice. In the end she exposes the dynasty at cost of her anonymity, choosing memory over erasure.
about_author: C. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former compliance investigator who spent a decade inside financial institutions before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about paper trails, quiet people, and the violence hidden in paperwork.

chapters.title: The Unattributed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She takes a routine missing-persons-adjacent job in Geneva, establishing her exile from three agencies and her talent for work no one wants on record. The emotional beat is weary competence masking shame.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: A lawyer hires Paloma: a client's sister was aboard a charter flight whose records vanished while it was still in the air. Paloma pulls the raw ADS-B data and finds a clean hole—sixty minutes of nothing. Beat: cold fascination.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She interviews an air traffic controller who remembers the plane but finds his own logs altered. Someone with institutional reach is rewriting reality. Beat: first real fear.

chapters.title: The Voss File
chapters.summary: Interlude from an unnamed watcher's POV, reporting to a patron that 'the analyst' has taken the bait. Readers learn Paloma is being observed before she does. Beat: dramatic irony and dread.

chapters.title: Three Generations of Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma traces the jet's ownership shell company to the Aldermann banking family, whose fortune survived wars by never appearing anywhere. Beat: the inheritance theme surfaces—the dead dictating the living.

chapters.title: Burned Twice
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Paloma was bounced from her second agency after refusing to bury a finding. Told partly in her own recollection as she drinks alone. Beat: self-loathing and stubbornness.

chapters.title: Elias Voss
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She locates Voss, the defector who claims he can prove what Flight 4471 carried: ledgers proving the Aldermann fortune was built on wartime theft. He is charming, frightened, and possibly lying. Beat: wary attraction.

chapters.title: What the Plane Carried
chapters.summary: Voss shows Paloma photographs of microfilmed ledgers allegedly aboard the flight. The manifest listed him as a passenger—but he never boarded. Beat: the trap's shape becomes visible.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Paloma scouts the French-Swiss border crossing where Voss must be moved, mapping shift changes and blind spots. Interleaved with the watcher reporting her movements. Beat: methodical tension tightening.

chapters.title: The Second Analyst
chapters.summary: Paloma discovers another analyst, Devi Rao, was assigned the same flight and then disappeared into a psychiatric hold. Visiting Devi, she hears a warning: 'They don't kill you. They erase you.' Beat: horror of institutional power.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marta Aldermann, elderly matriarch, reviewing the family's response to the defector problem with her security chief. She speaks of legacy like scripture. Beat: chilling intimacy with the antagonist.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Paloma moves Voss to a safehouse; he confesses part of his past—a betrayal that got a colleague killed—and asks why she believes him. She doesn't answer honestly. Beat: vulnerability under tradecraft.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Paloma's own records begin vanishing: bank accounts frozen, her lease terminated, her name dropped from databases. The machinery that erased the flight turns on her. Beat: existential vertigo.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Devi, released, contacts Paloma: the pattern matches an operation called LURE—defectors used to identify sympathizers. Is Voss bait? Paloma must decide whether to abort. Beat: agonizing doubt.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Jetty
chapters.summary: Paloma tests Voss with false information; his reaction proves he's been fed details only the watchers know. Confrontation on Lake Geneva: he admits he agreed to be bait to save his daughter. Beat: betrayal and pity entwined.

chapters.title: Marta's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marta Aldermann POV: she orders the checkpoint operation accelerated, revealing the family's true fear—not the ledgers, but a living witness who remembers her father's crimes. Beat: the theme of memory as threat.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Paloma devises the extraction: use the checkpoint's ninety-second shift change, a laundry truck, and Devi running interference digitally. Every piece must hold. Beat: taut preparation, rising hope.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: The extraction goes wrong—Voss freezes, a guard recognizes Paloma, shots are fired. She drags Voss through on instinct and grit, wounded. Beat: climax begins, adrenaline and terror.

chapters.title: The Long Field
chapters.summary: Pursuit across farmland at night toward a waiting contact. Voss saves Paloma's life in turn, repaying his debt. Beat: redemption earned in mud and blood.

chapters.title: Everything at Once
chapters.summary: Climax: Paloma releases the ledgers, flight data, and her own full testimony simultaneously to forty outlets—refusing to be erased quietly. Marta's network collapses as exposure cascades. Beat: cathartic detonation.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Aftermath: hearings begin, Devi is vindicated, Voss reunites with his daughter. Paloma, publicly named at last, discovers visibility is its own strange freedom. Beat: grief and relief mixed.

chapters.title: The Ghost of Geneva
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Paloma's POV. Months later she keeps the case files others won't touch, but now signs her name. A new client arrives with an impossible story; she listens. Beat: quiet resolve—memory chosen over invisibility.
